D009_m001.question:
It’s been about a year now that I’ve mostly felt…blank. Not exactly sad all the time, more like hollow. Stuff I used to care about—PT, range days, grabbing beers with the guys—just doesn’t register. I drag myself through duty, but even small tasks feel like I’m moving through mud. My body feels heavy all the time, and I get worn out just walking between buildings. Off duty I mostly go back to my room and lie there, staring at my phone without really seeing anything.

There’ve been moments where I’ll be standing near a balcony or crossing a road and this really strong urge hits me to just step off or walk into traffic. It scares me because it feels sudden and weirdly tempting, even though I don’t actually want to die.

What’s confusing is that about a month last spring I was the opposite—on top of the world. I barely slept and didn’t care; I’d go from the gym to planning new projects to messaging people nonstop. I couldn’t shut up, talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one idea to another. I was constantly restless, pacing, needing to be doing something. My sex drive went through the roof—I was swiping, sexting, hooking up whenever I could. I still did my job fine, but I was “on” all the time, almost too much.
D009_m001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m002.question:
For about a year now I’ve been in this really low place that I can’t seem to shake. I go to clinic, but it feels mechanical. I used to love tricky derm cases, journal clubs, even teaching residents. Now I just…don’t care. When I get home, I crash on the couch. Even taking a shower feels like lifting weights. I’m constantly exhausted, heavy, and most weekends I just lie in bed scrolling or staring at the ceiling.

My mood is mostly flat or down, and there are days I think my family would be better off without me. I’ve caught myself planning it out in detail—where I’d do it, how to make it look like an accident so my kids remember me as “the good mom doctor.” That scares me, but it also feels strangely…organized.

Before this long slump, about a year ago, I had a month where I was “on fire.” I was snapping at my husband over tiny things but also buzzing with energy—working late, starting new clinic protocols, rewriting patient brochures at 2–3 a.m. I’d sleep maybe two hours and feel like I didn’t need more. My colleagues joked I was “turbo-charged.” I talked nonstop in meetings; it felt unbearable to slow down or tolerate silence. Then that faded, and I dropped into this long, drained, gray phase I’m still stuck in.
D009_m002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m003.question:
For about a year now, I’ve felt…hollow is the best word. I go through the motions at the firm, but even when I win a case, it barely registers. My partners congratulate me and I just nod; it doesn’t mean anything. I’m exhausted all the time. Weekends, I can sleep ten, twelve hours and still wake up feeling like I’ve run a marathon. I’ve cut way back on my caseload because I just can’t keep up.

I’ve also had some pretty dark thoughts. I’ve caught myself planning it out in detail—where I’d do it, how to make sure my ex-wife and kids wouldn’t be the ones to find me, what I’d write in a note. It’s not just vague “I wish I were gone”; it’s concrete.

Then there was this stretch about a month long, a few months back, where I felt almost unnaturally good. I was buzzing with energy, barely slept and didn’t miss it, took on extra files, started drafting a book, reorganized the entire apartment at 3 a.m. I was talking nonstop in meetings, pacing around my office, couldn’t sit still. I felt fantastic—but looking back, it was…off.
D009_m003.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m004.question:
Over the past year, it feels like I’ve been two different people.

Most of the time, I feel hollow, like someone turned the volume down on my life. I sit at my desk, stare at emails or lesson plans, and just…can’t start. Things that used to energize me—meeting with teachers, planning programs—now feel overwhelming. My mind tires so quickly; after a short meeting I’m mentally drained, like I’ve run a marathon in my head. I go through the motions at school, but at home I mostly sit in silence. I’ve caught myself thinking that everyone would be better off without me, or that I just want it all to stop, though I haven’t made any concrete plans.

Then there was this stretch about a month long, a few months back, where I was oddly “revved up.” I slept maybe three, four hours a night and still woke up buzzing. I couldn’t sit still—pacing in my office, rearranging things, starting new initiatives. I was snapping at staff over small issues, talking nonstop in meetings, jumping from idea to idea. I got a lot done, but I could tell people were a bit taken aback by how intense I was.
D009_m004.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m005.question:
It’s been a rough year. For most of the past twelve months I’ve felt like I’m moving through wet concrete. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—work, watching the game, even spending time with my wife and kids just feels flat. I drag myself to the plant, but checking parts that used to be second nature now wears me out mentally within an hour. I make stupid mistakes, and then I just stare at the paperwork because my brain feels empty and exhausted.

My mood is low pretty much every day. It’s not just being “down,” it’s like there’s no point to anything. Sometimes, when I’m driving over an overpass or walking by the road, I get these sudden urges, like, “What if I just went over?” I haven’t made a plan, but those thoughts scare me.

What’s confusing is that about a year ago, for maybe a month, I felt the opposite—on top of the world. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, and still felt wired. I was talking nonstop at work, super chatty with everyone, calling old friends, checking in on every line in the factory like I could do ten jobs at once. I knew I was more “up” than usual, but it didn’t really get me into trouble, so I just thought I was having a really good streak.
D009_m005.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m006.question:
Over the last few years, it’s felt like I swing between two completely different versions of myself, and it’s getting harder to predict.  

About four months ago, for almost two months straight, I felt like I was “on” all the time. Not exactly happy—more on edge and easily annoyed—but wired. I’d snap at staff for tiny mistakes, argue with clients over minor issues, then stay late at the branch because I was convinced I could push through three or four new initiatives at once. I was working nonstop, pacing in my office, talking faster than usual. On the way home I was driving way too aggressively, cutting it close with lights, taking stupid chances I normally wouldn’t. My wife kept telling me to slow down, that I was being intense and short-tempered.  

Then it crashed. For the past two months I’ve felt flat, like everything is muted. I go to bed at a decent hour and technically sleep enough, but I wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all. I’m dragging myself to work, just going through the motions, and it’s starting to affect how I manage my team and even basic tasks. At home, I’m just… there, but not really present.
D009_m006.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m007.question:
It kind of comes in waves. About four months ago I had this stretch, maybe two months, where I felt… wired, I guess. I’d be on shift and just buzzing, talking non‑stop, volunteering for extra patrols, extra reports, extra details. I was starting new initiatives, rewriting procedures, staying late, then hitting the gym after. I barely sat still at home either—cleaning the garage at midnight, planning home projects. My mood would flip fast: one minute I’d be joking around, feeling on top of the world, and the next I’d snap at my partner or my wife over nothing.

During that time I also did some things I’m not proud of—texting and meeting up with a woman I met on a call. That’s not something I’ve ever done before, and it scared me afterward.

Then, almost like a switch, the bottom dropped out. For about the last two months I’ve felt low, heavy. I sleep enough hours but wake up exhausted, like I didn’t rest at all. I’m dragging myself to work, missing details, avoiding buddies, snapping at my kids, and my wife says I’m just a shell of myself. It’s getting hard to function.
D009_m007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m008.question:
I guess this all really kicked off around eight months ago. I go through these stretches where I’m just… switched on. For like a couple of months I’m buzzing. I’ll wake up after four, five hours of sleep and feel wired, not tired at all. I take extra shifts, stay late at the site, start side projects at home—rewiring my mate’s place, sketching out business ideas. I’m talking non‑stop, messaging people I haven’t seen in years, going out most nights even when I’ve got work at 6 a.m.  

My mood flips fast though. One minute I’m on top of the world, joking around, the next I’m snappy and picking fights over nothing. I’ve done some really stupid stuff in those times—driving way too fast, messing around with gear at parties, not really caring what could happen.  

Then it’s like a switch goes the other way. For the next couple of months, everything feels flat and distant, like I’m watching my life from behind glass. I can sleep 12 hours and still crash on the couch after work. Lately it’s been so bad I’ve been calling in sick, falling behind with my apprenticeship jobs, just not able to make myself care about anything.
D009_m008.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m009.question:
It’s been a strange few months. About four months ago I had this stretch, maybe a good two months, where I just felt amazing for no real reason. I’d wake up buzzing with energy, like I’d had three coffees, even if I hadn’t slept that well. At work, I was flying through tasks, taking on extra routes, reorganizing schedules, suggesting new recycling projects on my own time. I couldn’t sit still in meetings—tapping my feet, getting up, walking around the depot. At home I’d pace around the house in the evenings, feeling like I had to keep moving.

I also started spending a lot. I ordered tools, gadgets, even a pricey mountain bike online without really thinking it through. My wife was pretty upset when the credit card bill came.

Then, about two months ago, that “high” just sort of dropped off. Since then I’ve mostly felt blank, like there’s nothing inside. I lie in bed at night, mind going in circles, but I can’t drift off for hours. Getting up for work is hard, and lately I’ve been calling in sick or just going through the motions when I do make it in.
D009_m009.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m010.question:
It kind of comes in waves. About four months ago I had this stretch, maybe two months, where I felt… amazing. Like, “on top of the world” amazing. I barely felt tired, I was bouncing around my classroom, taking on extra projects, staying up late planning new activities for my students and still waking up buzzing with energy. I was talking fast, had a million ideas at once, couldn’t sit still. My friends even joked I was “too happy,” like everything felt exciting for no real reason.

Around that same time, my sex drive just shot up out of nowhere. I was using dating apps a lot, going home with people I’d just met, which really isn’t like me. I wasn’t thinking it through, just chasing that rush.

Then it crashed. For the last two months I’ve been the opposite—really low, heavy. I can sleep 12 hours and still nap after school. Getting out of bed feels like dragging concrete. I’ve been calling in sick more, falling behind on IEPs, and cancelling on friends. It’s this persistent sadness and exhaustion I can’t shake.
D009_m010.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m011.question:
I’d say it really started about nine months ago. Most days I just feel…hollow, like I’m on autopilot. I go to work, drive my routes, come home, but there’s nothing going on inside. I’m exhausted all the time, even on days when I sleep a full night. I’ll be in bed by ten, up by six, but I wake up feeling like I never slept. My wife says I just drag myself around the house. On my days off I mostly lie on the couch; even small things like taking the kids to the park feel like too much.

Then there was this stretch about three weeks long a couple months back where I was the complete opposite. I barely sat still—pacing around, cleaning the house at midnight, planning side businesses, taking extra shifts. I was snapping at passengers and my coworkers over tiny things. I kept telling my wife I could handle anything, that I was smarter than my supervisors, that I should be running the whole depot. I wasn’t really sleeping much, but I didn’t feel tired then. After that, I crashed back into this numb, worn-out state.
D009_m011.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m012.question:
For most of this past year, I’ve felt like I’ve been running on empty. I’m usually very on top of things at the hospital, but for about nine months now I’ve just felt low and flat most days, like there’s a weight on me. Even when I sleep a full night, I wake up feeling as if I haven’t rested at all. By midday, just trying to keep track of orders or make a staffing plan feels exhausting, like thinking itself wears me out. I’ve been slower at work, more irritable at home, and my husband says I’m “not myself.” It’s gotten hard to keep up with the demands of being in charge of the ward.

Earlier this year, though, there was a stretch of about three weeks where I was the opposite. I was in a fantastic mood, almost giddy. I barely sat still—constantly pacing the unit, starting new projects, reorganizing schedules, volunteering for extra committees. I felt like I could run the whole hospital better than administration, like everything I touched would turn out brilliantly. I didn’t really slow down, even off shift. It didn’t exactly cause problems, but looking back it was like I was revved up too high.
D009_m012.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m013.question:
It’s been a rough stretch for about nine months now. Most days I just feel…flat or low. I drag myself to school, but standing in front of a class feels exhausting, like my whole body is made of sandbags. I used to stay after to help kids or coach debate; now I go straight home and lie on the couch. Even small things—doing dishes, grading—feel overwhelming.  

Sleep is a mess. I’ll fall asleep okay, then wake up at 2 or 3 a.m. and just stare at the ceiling for an hour or two, worrying about lessons, bills, my future. By the time the alarm goes off, I feel like I haven’t slept at all.  

What’s confusing is that, about three weeks ago, I had this stretch where I suddenly felt “on.” I was snapping at students and colleagues over tiny things, but also buzzing with energy—rewriting the whole semester’s curriculum in one night, starting side projects, messaging multiple people on dating apps. I kept thinking I was meant for something huge, like I was wasting my talent just teaching. My sex drive shot up too; I was flirting a lot more than usual. I still made it to work and got things done, but it felt like I was revved way too high.
D009_m013.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m014.question:
It’s been a rough year. For about the last nine months, I’ve mostly felt…blank. Not sad exactly, more like hollow. I go to school, stand in front of my classes, but I feel disconnected, like I’m on autopilot. By the time I get home, I’m wiped out, even on days that aren’t busy. No matter how much I rest on weekends, the tiredness never really lifts. 

Nights are the worst. I’ll go to bed at a reasonable time, but I just lie there, staring at the ceiling, my mind not even racing—just empty—and it can take hours to drift off. That’s started to affect my teaching; I’m slower with grading, forgetting things I normally wouldn’t, avoiding taking on anything extra. My wife says I seem far away, like I’m not really there with the family.

What’s confusing is that about a year ago I had this three‑week stretch where I felt incredible—full of energy, talking to everyone, taking on new projects at school, convinced I was meant to make some huge impact on education. I barely sat still. Then it just faded, and since then it’s been this long, dragging numbness.
D009_m014.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m015.question:
I guess the main thing is that I feel like two different people depending on the phase I’m in.

For most of the last nine months, I’ve been dragging myself through the day. It’s like someone turned the volume down on all my feelings. Things that should make me happy—my kids’ soccer games, finishing a project at work—just feel flat. My body feels like it weighs a ton. Even walking up the stairs at home feels like too much sometimes. I get home from the plant and just collapse on the couch. I’m missing deadlines, avoiding meetings, my wife says I’m “there but not really there.” At night I lie in bed for hours, mind blank but unable to actually fall asleep.

Then, about three weeks ago, it flipped. I suddenly had all this energy. I barely sat still—cleaning the garage at midnight, sketching designs for some big invention I’m convinced will change our industry. I felt unstoppable, like I could do anything and everyone else was just too slow. I got snappy over tiny things, especially with coworkers and my wife. My sex drive shot up to the point it was awkward—I was pressuring my wife more than usual, and even catching myself flirting at work, which is not like me. It didn’t exactly wreck my life, but it scared her, and looking back, it doesn’t feel normal.
D009_m015.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m016.question:
It’s been a rough few months. For about four months now I’ve felt mostly low… like there’s a cloud over everything. I wake up dreading the day, and even simple things like making dinner or going out to collect census forms feel overwhelming. I’ve cut my hours back because I just can’t push myself. I keep thinking my husband would be better off without me, that I’m just dead weight. Sometimes at night I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.

I also feel like my mind doesn’t work the way it used to. I misplace my clipboard or keys constantly and lose my train of thought mid-sentence, which makes me feel stupid.

What’s strange is that about three weeks before this long slump, I had a spell where I was “up.” I was buzzing with energy, talking fast, starting projects all over the house, taking on extra census routes. My mood flipped quickly from excited to snappy over small things, and I’d jump from one task to another without finishing anything. It didn’t exactly ruin my life, but it felt… off, not like my normal self.
D009_m016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009_m017.question:
It’s been about four months now where I’ve just felt…flat or worse. I cry a lot, sometimes over nothing specific—like I’ll just be reading an email from my advisor and suddenly I’m in tears. Things I used to enjoy—my research, seeing friends, even just watching stupid shows—feel like they’re behind glass. I go through the motions, but I don’t feel anything good from it.

I keep replaying small mistakes in my head, like missing a deadline or not answering an email right away, and I feel like I’ve ruined everything. I tell myself I’m a burden, that I don’t deserve to be here. I have these thoughts about not wanting to exist anymore, like it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, but I haven’t made any plans.

My concentration is terrible. I reread the same paragraph over and over and nothing sticks, so my coursework and thesis have really suffered. 

Before this, there was this three‑week period where I barely slept, felt weirdly “on,” jumping from idea to idea, talking fast, starting projects I never finished. My mood would swing from super excited to snapping at people for no reason, but I was still going to class and getting things done.
D009_m017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009_m018.question:
It’s been about four months now where I’ve just…crashed. Before that there was this three‑week stretch where I felt weirdly “on.” I was sleeping less but didn’t feel tired, bouncing around my apartment, sketching nonstop. I couldn’t sit still; if I tried to rest my legs would shake and I’d pace while my tablet was exporting. My mood kept snapping from “this is the best story ever, I’m a genius” to snapping at my editor over tiny comments. Every little sound—the fridge, traffic, my phone lighting up—pulled my attention away, but I still somehow met my weekly uploads.

After that, everything flipped. Now I wake up and just start crying for no clear reason. Drawing used to be my escape, but lately even opening my sketch app feels pointless. I stare at the panels and think, “Why bother? I’m useless, anyone could do this better.” It’s hard to focus long enough to read a script email or follow a show; my mind just drifts. I’ve been having these repeating thoughts like, “I wish I just wouldn’t wake up,” or “It’d be easier if I disappeared,” but I haven’t made any plans or anything. It’s gotten so bad I’ve missed deadlines and had to push back episodes.
D009_m018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009_m019.question:
It’s been a weird back-and-forth year. About five months ago I slipped into this long low patch that’s still kind of going on, maybe four months solid. I feel…blank most of the time. Not sad exactly, just like someone turned the volume down on everything. Wins at work don’t mean anything—I’ll finish a campaign that does really well and I just stare at the numbers like, “Who cares.”

What’s been freaking me out is this constant sense that I’ve ruined people’s lives. If I hear about an accident or some bad news on the radio, I get stuck on the idea that it’s somehow my fault—like because I complained about something that day, I caused it. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels true.  

My brain’s molasses. I reread the same sentence over and over, zone out in meetings, can’t follow shows. I’ve actually mapped out how I’d end things—where, what I’d use, even what I’d schedule on social so posts go out after I’m gone.

Then about three weeks this summer I was the total opposite—running on turbo. I barely slept, had endless ideas, was snappy with everyone, jumping at every notification or noise, like everything was demanding my attention at once. I still got my work done, but I was on edge and couldn’t sit still.
D009_m019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009_m020.question:
I guess this all really started about four months ago. My mood just dropped and never really came back up. I fly less now because I’m struggling to function day to day. I feel…flat, heavy, like everything’s an effort. When I’m home, I mostly stay in the bedroom or on the couch. My wife keeps asking what’s wrong because I avoid family dinners, friends, all of it. I just don’t have it in me.

I obsess over little mistakes I’ve made—things from flights years ago that turned out fine, something sharp I said to my kids—and I replay them over and over, telling myself I’m a terrible husband and father. Even simple choices feel overwhelming—what to eat, what shirt to wear. I stare at the closet for ten minutes and still can’t decide. 

Most nights I fall asleep thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning anything, but the idea of just…not being here feels like a relief.

About a year ago I had almost the opposite for three weeks—barely sleeping, constantly on the move, short-tempered in the cockpit, snapping at colleagues over nothing, jumping from task to task, distracted by every little noise in the cabin. But I still kept everything going then. This time, I can’t.
D009_m020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D009_m021.question:
I’ve been on the road most of my life, so I’m used to long hours and weird sleep, but this last year or so something’s been really off.

For a little over a year now, most days I just feel…flat and low. I used to enjoy talking with other drivers at truck stops, listening to podcasts, tinkering with my pickup on weekends. Now I just don’t care. My wife asks me simple things and I just sit there a bit before I answer, like my brain’s moving through mud. Even climbing in and out of the cab feels like I’ve got weights on me. I’m tired all the time, and the sadness just kind of hangs there all day. It’s gotten hard to keep up with runs and house stuff.

But then, about three months ago, I had this stretch where I flipped the other way. I was in a great mood one minute, then snapping at dispatch or my wife the next. I couldn’t sit still—cleaning the truck, planning new routes, starting projects at home between hauls. I’d go several nights barely sleeping and it didn’t bother me; I’d just keep driving, talking, doing things. It didn’t exactly wreck my work, but it felt like I was revving too high all the time, and then I crashed back into this low again.
D009_m021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m022.question:
It’s been a strange few years. About a year ago, I slipped into this… heaviness. It’s still going on, really. I used to be so proud of my students, my work, but now even when someone tells me, “You changed my life,” I just feel blank, like it happened to someone else. Everything I do feels slow—getting dressed, making tea, even walking around the house. My husband keeps asking if I’m in pain, but it’s more like I’m moving through mud.

Thinking wears me out. Reading a page of a book, balancing the checkbook—my mind gets tired so quickly I just give up. I cry over little things: a commercial, a song, even folding my old lesson plans. It’s embarrassing, and I’ve stopped going to my book club and church group because it’s too much effort and I’m afraid I’ll start crying there too.

What’s confusing is that before this long slump, there was a stretch—maybe three months—where I felt oddly “wired”: bouncing between feeling on top of the world and snapping at my husband over nothing, full of energy, barely sleeping and not even minding it. But this last year has really knocked the wind out of me.
D009_m022.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m023.question:
It’s been a weird couple of years, like I live in two totally different versions of myself.

The “up” stretches started maybe three months ago and lasted around that long. I’d wake up after four, five hours of sleep and feel completely wired, like I’d had three coffees. My brain would be buzzing with ideas for character voices, demo reels, branding, networking emails. I’d record all night, reorganize my whole portfolio at 3 a.m., clean my apartment, go for a run. I was talking fast, jumping from project to project, just this constant go-go-go, but I was actually getting more auditions done, so I didn’t think it was a problem.

The “down” side has been going on for over a year. That’s when it feels like everything’s hollow. I stop caring about voice work, stop gaming, stop seeing friends. I pace my apartment, pick at my skin, can’t sit through a script read without my mind burning out after a few lines. Even answering emails feels exhausting. I miss deadlines, cancel gigs, and just feel…blank, like there’s nothing inside, just going through motions because I have to pay rent.

D009_m024.question:
It’s been a strange couple of years. About a year ago, I just sank. I stopped enjoying anything — even walking through the halls and chatting with the kids felt pointless. I drag myself around the building; teachers have commented that I’m “moving in slow motion.” Just climbing the stairs to a classroom feels like wading through mud. D009_m025.question:

Little things would set me off; if someone on my team was slow or questioned me, I’d snap or feel instantly furious. I kept functioning, but I knew I was kind of “too much,” even for me.

D009_m026.question:

It kind of goes in waves for me. 

About seven months ago I had this stretch, maybe a month long, where I felt amazing. Like, almost too good. I was waking up before my alarm, buzzing with energy, cranking out campaigns, rewriting whole content calendars overnight. I’d start three new ideas before I finished the first one—new side projects, a podcast concept, an online course. My brain just wouldn’t shut up; it felt like ten tabs open at once. I’d be pacing around my apartment while “working,” talking to myself, unable to sit still, but I was still hitting deadlines so no one at work really complained.

Then it crashed. For the last six months it’s been the opposite. I feel hollow most of the time—like I’m there but not really feeling anything. I’ve been dodging friends’ texts, making excuses to avoid going out. Even simple tasks—writing a short post, answering emails—feel exhausting. I reread the same sentence three times and it doesn’t stick. I come home and just lie on the couch staring at my phone. I keep having these thoughts like, “What’s the point?” and sometimes, “It’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up,” though I haven’t planned anything. It’s starting to affect my job performance and I’m scared I’m going to lose it.

For the past four months, I’ve mostly felt like I’m dragging myself through the day. I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling, like there’s no point to anything. I’ve been calling in sick a lot, missing targets, and my numbers at work have tanked. Talking to clients used to come naturally, but now even picking up the phone feels exhausting. I dodge meetings, avoid my colleagues, and at home I mostly stay in the bedroom, barely talking to my wife.

I keep replaying small mistakes—like snapping at a customer or forgetting to send an email—and I feel like a terrible husband and a useless provider. It’s way out of proportion, but I can’t shake the thought that my family would be better off without me. I don’t have a plan, but thoughts like “maybe it’d be easier if I just wasn’t here” pop up almost every day.

Before this, about a month or so, I was the opposite—wired. I was up late, pacing around, constantly on the move, making calls, networking, scheduling drinks with clients and old friends. I was sharper with people, but also on edge, snapping over tiny things—traffic, my wife being five minutes late. I couldn’t sit still, but I wasn’t falling apart like I am now.

    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m047.question:
It’s been a weird couple of years. For about a month at a time I’ll get into these stretches where I feel “switched on.” I’m bouncing between feeling almost giddy and then suddenly snappy or irritated over nothing. I’ll pace around my apartment, walk laps while I’m on the phone, tap my fingers nonstop. I can’t sit through a full TV episode. I start three articles in a night, reorganize my bookshelf at 2 a.m.—it’s not even productive half the time, I’m just…driven and restless.

Then it flips. The last bad slump lasted around four months. It’s like someone unplugged me. I sit in front of my laptop and just stare; even answering simple emails feels impossible. I don’t really feel sad exactly—more like empty, like everything is behind glass. I replay every small mistake, every missed deadline after the divorce, and convince myself I’ve ruined my life and my son’s. A few months ago I stockpiled my anxiety meds and wrote goodbye letters. I didn’t go through with it, obviously, but I wanted to. I barely worked during that time and almost lost my main client.
D009_m047.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m048.question:
It’s been a strange few months. About five months ago I slipped into this…hollow place. I wake up feeling like there’s nothing inside me, just a sort of blank heaviness. I used to enjoy gardening and knitting for the grandkids, but for about four months now I haven’t cared about any of it. Most days I sit in my chair and stare at the TV without really watching. I keep thinking my life doesn’t amount to much, that I’m just taking up space since my husband died. Some nights I go to bed hoping I just won’t wake up, not that I’d do anything to make that happen, but the thought is there a lot.

Then, about a month ago, things flipped. I suddenly had this rush of energy, barely needed sleep, buzzing around the house cleaning cupboards at 3 a.m. I felt unusually cheerful, almost giddy, like everything was brighter. I even found myself thinking about sex far more than is normal for me at my age, browsing dating sites and feeling a bit…revved up. I’ve managed my daily tasks, but it all feels out of character and unsettling.

    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m049.question:
For the last four months or so, I’ve felt like I’m moving through sludge. I get up, go to the firm, but it’s all mechanical. Wins in court, good settlements—things that used to matter—barely register. It all feels hollow, like there’s nothing inside. My ex-wife says I should be proud of how far I’ve come, but I just don’t care. 

When I’m alone, especially at night, my mind locks onto every misstep I’ve made—cases I could’ve argued better, things I said to my kids during the divorce. I replay them endlessly and beat myself up. I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up one morning. I’m not planning anything, but the idea of not having to keep going sometimes feels like a relief. It’s gotten hard to concentrate, and I’ve cut my hours because I just can’t keep up.

About a month before this slump started, I was the opposite—wired, snappy over small things, barely sleeping but full of energy, working nonstop, flirting excessively, even having more sex than usual. It didn’t really mess up my work, but I knew I was “amped up” in a way that didn’t feel normal.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m050.question:
It’s been a rough few months. The first thing that really threw me was this stretch about a month long where I felt…amped up, but not in a good way. At work I’m usually pretty even, but I started snapping at people over tiny things—an email phrased wrong, a delay in a report—and then feeling like I couldn’t sit still. I’d pace the halls between meetings, tapping my fingers, rearranging things on my desk over and over without really needing to. I was constantly busy but not actually getting more done.

Then it sort of flipped. For the past four months I’ve been sinking. I cry at my desk, in the bathroom, on the drive home, and half the time I can’t say why. Stuff I used to enjoy—grabbing drinks with friends, even just watching a show—feels flat, like I’m just going through motions. I keep replaying small mistakes at the hospital and convincing myself I’ve harmed patients indirectly, that I don’t deserve this job. I’ve thought a lot about ending things, down to where I would go and how I’d do it, and that scares me. It’s gotten hard to keep up at work. I’m behind on emails, avoiding meetings, and calling in sick more than I ever have.
